purpose: reading-comprehension items; the contradicted item is composed by the pipeline from basis+alter and always shown with its label

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Across multiple cancer types, IFI35 expression correlated positively with infiltration levels of mast cells, neutrophils, eosinophils, CD4+ T cell subtypes and cancer-associated fibroblasts.
statements.evidence: IFI35 expression was positively associated with increased infiltration levels of mast cells, neutrophils, eosinophils, CD4+ T cell subtypes, and cancer-associated fibroblasts across multiple cancer types.
statements.note: The abstract reports a positive association between IFI35 expression and infiltration of these immune and stromal cell types, not a negative one.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: IFI35 was significantly upregulated at both mRNA and protein levels in several cancers, with the most pronounced increase in breast cancer.
statements.evidence: IFI35 expression was significantly upregulated at both messenger RNA and protein levels in multiple cancers, most prominently in BRCA
statements.note: The abstract states that IFI35 upregulation at mRNA and protein level was seen across multiple cancers and was most prominent in BRCA.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Silencing IFI35 made BRCA cells more sensitive to chemotherapeutic drugs.
statements.evidence: Functional studies demonstrated that IFI35 knockdown effectively suppressed BRCA cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while promoting apoptosis.
statements.note: The knockdown experiments measured proliferation, migration, invasion and apoptosis; no drug treatment or chemosensitivity result is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Depleting IFI35 significantly slowed xenograft tumor growth in nude mice.
statements.evidence: In vivo, IFI35 depletion significantly inhibited xenograft tumor growth.
statements.note: The abstract reports that IFI35 depletion significantly inhibited tumor growth in the nude mouse xenograft model.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Sensitivity of postoperative ctDNA detection was similar at day 14 and day 30 (31% versus 32%), with 98% specificity at both timepoints.
statements.evidence: performance was comparable between the two timepoints (sensitivity, 31% vs. 32% and specificity, both 98%)
statements.note: The abstract gives sensitivities of 31% and 32% and a specificity of 98% at both timepoints.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Among ctDNA-positive patients, those who started adjuvant chemotherapy early had a lower recurrence rate than those who started later.
statements.evidence: Combining the timepoints would increase sensitivity (36%) and allow earlier ACT start in 80% of patients.
statements.note: The abstract discusses how early ACT could be allocated but reports no comparison of recurrence between patients treated early and late.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Capping cfDNA input at 50 ng lowered the probability of detecting ctDNA, affecting 78% of day 14 and 65% of day 30 samples.
statements.evidence: A 50-ng cfDNA input cap reduced ctDNA detection probability, affecting 78% of day 14 samples and 65% of day 30 samples.
statements.note: The abstract reports that a 50-ng input cap reduced detection probability in 78% of day 14 and 65% of day 30 samples.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: A rise in ctDNA level between day 14 and day 30 was associated with a shorter time to recurrence.
statements.evidence: An increase in the ctDNA level from day 14 to day 30 was associated with a shorter time to recurrence (Pearson R = -0.63, P = 0.003).
statements.note: The abstract reports that an increase in ctDNA from day 14 to day 30 was associated with a shorter, not longer, time to recurrence.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Organoids established from malignant pleural effusions carried a higher tumor mutation burden than those derived from resected tumors.
statements.evidence: Early and locally advanced-stage tumor-derived LCOs exhibited higher TMB and MSI compared to those from advanced-stage disease
statements.note: TMB is compared by disease stage only; the abstract never compares organoids from pleural effusions with those from resected tumors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Roughly 80% of the somatic variants found in the organoids lay in non-coding regions of the genome.
statements.evidence: with approximately 80% of somatic variants located in non-coding regions
statements.note: The abstract states that approximately 80% of somatic variants were located in non-coding regions.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Organoids from early and locally advanced-stage tumors showed higher TMB and MSI than organoids from advanced-stage disease.
statements.evidence: Early and locally advanced-stage tumor-derived LCOs exhibited higher TMB and MSI compared to those from advanced-stage disease
statements.note: The abstract reports higher, not lower, TMB and MSI in organoids from early and locally advanced-stage tumors compared with advanced-stage disease.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Whole-genome sequencing of the organoids identified recurrent mutations in TP53, TTN, MUC16 and FLG.
statements.evidence: WGS revealed recurrent mutations in TP53 , TTN , MUC16 , and FLG
statements.note: The abstract lists TP53, TTN, MUC16 and FLG as recurrently mutated genes in the organoids.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Using a score of 3 or more as the cutoff, the scoring system identified peripheral blood EGFR positivity with 84.8% sensitivity and 73.1% specificity.
statements.evidence: A score of ≥3 was considered a high-probability population with positive EGFR in peripheral blood. The sensitivity for diagnosing positive EGFR in peripheral blood was 84.8%, and the specificity was 73.1%.
statements.note: The abstract defines a score of 3 or more as high probability and reports 84.8% sensitivity and 73.1% specificity for blood EGFR positivity.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The model predicting EGFR positivity in peripheral blood had an area under the curve of 0.884.
statements.evidence: the area under the curve (AUC) was 0.884
statements.note: The abstract reports an AUC of 0.884 for the peripheral blood EGFR prediction model.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: With NGS as the reference standard, ARMS-PCR detected EGFR mutations with 94.96% sensitivity and 100% specificity.
statements.evidence: the sensitivity of amplification refractory mutation system polymerase chain reaction (ARMS-PCR) detection was 94.96%, the specificity was 100%
statements.note: The abstract reports 94.96% sensitivity and 100% specificity for ARMS-PCR against NGS as reference.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The scoring system's performance was confirmed in an independent external validation cohort.
statements.evidence: Univariate and binary logistic regression analyses were conducted to establish a predictive model for EGFR in peripheral blood, which was subsequently converted into a scoring system.
statements.note: The abstract describes building the model and its performance in the 384-patient cohort; no external or independent validation is mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: About 74% of the pear lncRNAs overlapped with transposable elements.
statements.evidence: Roughly 74% of lncRNAs overlapped with transposable elements (TEs)
statements.note: The abstract states that roughly 74% of lncRNAs overlapped with TEs.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transgenic overexpression of lncRNA-pys raised lignin content in pear.
statements.evidence: demonstrating that overexpressing lncRNA-pys led to an increase in lignin content in pear
statements.note: The abstract reports that overexpressing lncRNA-pys in transgenic experiments increased lignin content.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Most of the TE-overlapping lncRNAs were derived from long terminal repeat retrotransposons.
statements.evidence: Roughly 74% of lncRNAs overlapped with transposable elements (TEs) and significantly impacted sequence diversity, expression variation, and tissue-specific expression.
statements.note: The abstract gives the fraction of lncRNAs overlapping TEs but says nothing about which TE classes are involved.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The 12 422 identified lncRNAs showed higher tissue specificity and lower sequence conservation than protein-coding genes.
statements.evidence: identified 12 422 lncRNAs that exhibited higher tissue specificity and lower sequence conservation than protein-coding genes
statements.note: The abstract reports that the lncRNAs had lower, not higher, sequence conservation than protein-coding genes.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: At diagnosis, copy-number alterations were detectable in CSF cell-free DNA from 89% of patients.
statements.evidence: Among the diagnostic samples, CNAs were detected in samples from 17/19 patients (89%), which included 8 with marker-negative tumors.
statements.note: The abstract reports CNA detection in 17 of 19 patients sampled at diagnosis, that is 89%.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: CSF ctDNA was detected more often in non-germinomatous germ cell tumors than in germinomas.
statements.evidence: Among the diagnostic samples, CNAs were detected in samples from 17/19 patients (89%), which included 8 with marker-negative tumors.
statements.note: Detection is reported for the whole diagnostic cohort; the abstract gives no comparison between germinoma and non-germinomatous tumors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The sequenced cohort comprised 29 CSF samples from 21 patients, 16 with germinoma and 5 with non-germinomatous GCT.
statements.evidence: A total of 29 CSF samples from 21 patients (16 with germinoma, 5 with non-germinomatous GCT) were sequenced.
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly these numbers: 29 samples, 21 patients, 16 germinoma and 5 non-germinomatous GCT.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Eight of the patients with CNAs detected in diagnostic CSF had tumors that were negative for tumor markers.
statements.evidence: Among the diagnostic samples, CNAs were detected in samples from 17/19 patients (89%), which included 8 with marker-negative tumors.
statements.note: The abstract states that the 17 patients with CNAs at diagnosis included 8 with marker-negative tumors.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mean cfDNA concentration in CSF was 84.9 ng/ml in CNS tumor patients compared with 5.7 ng/ml in controls.
statements.evidence: CNS tumors had significantly greater cfDNA concentration in the CSF (mean 84.9 ± 340.9 ng/ml vs 5.7 ± 8.1 ng/ml in controls, p = 0.004)
statements.note: The abstract reports mean CSF cfDNA concentrations of 84.9 ng/ml in tumor patients and 5.7 ng/ml in controls.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The regression model estimated that collecting 3.35 ml of CSF gives a 90% success rate for the NGS assay.
statements.evidence: 80%, 85%, and 90% success rates for NGS assay require collection of 0.70 ml, 1.26 ml, 3.35 ml of CSF, respectively
statements.note: The abstract pairs 3.35 ml of CSF with a 90% NGS success rate; 0.70 ml and 1.26 ml correspond to 80% and 85%.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Shunt tap samples yielded less cfDNA than samples collected at dural opening.
statements.evidence: The cfDNA yield and concentration were comparable between the dural opening and ventricular catheter cohorts.
statements.note: Only the dural opening and ventricular catheter cohorts are compared; the abstract reports no cfDNA result for the shunt tap samples.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: cfDNA yield and concentration were comparable between CSF collected at dural opening and CSF drawn from a ventricular catheter.
statements.evidence: The cfDNA yield and concentration were comparable between the dural opening and ventricular catheter cohorts.
statements.note: The abstract states that yield and concentration were comparable between the dural opening and ventricular catheter cohorts.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Female patients experienced more immune-related adverse events than male patients.
statements.evidence: We found that male patients exhibited better immunotherapy outcomes and higher tumor mutational burden.
statements.note: Outcomes here refer to treatment efficacy; the abstract reports nothing about adverse events or toxicity in either sex.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Male patients had better immunotherapy outcomes and a higher tumor mutational burden.
statements.evidence: We found that male patients exhibited better immunotherapy outcomes and higher tumor mutational burden.
statements.note: The abstract reports better immunotherapy outcomes and higher tumor mutational burden in male, not female, patients.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of 68 significantly mutated genes associated with immunotherapy outcomes, nine showed gender differences.
statements.evidence: 68 significantly mutated genes were identified to be associated with immunotherapy outcomes, with nine genes (i.e., ATM, ATRX, DOT1L, EP300, EPHB1, NOTCH1, PBRM1, RBM10, and SETD2) exhibiting gender differences
statements.note: The abstract names 68 outcome-associated mutated genes and lists nine of them with gender differences.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Based on mutational activities, the study identified four molecular subtypes that differed by gender and related to treatment outcomes.
statements.evidence: Based on mutational activities, we identified four potential molecular subtypes with gender differences and relevance to treatment outcomes.
statements.note: The abstract reports four potential molecular subtypes derived from mutational activities, with gender differences and relevance to outcomes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: cgMLST separated the isolates into two genetic clusters, an ST307 cluster of five isolates and an ST101 cluster of two.
statements.evidence: Core genome multi-locus sequence typing analysis (cgMLST) identified two distinct genetic clusters: a sequence type (ST) 307 cluster (n = 5) and a ST101 cluster (n = 2).
statements.note: The abstract reports two cgMLST clusters, ST307 with five isolates and ST101 with two.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The transposon carrying blaKPC-3 belonged to the Tn4401 family.
statements.evidence: Here, a bla KPC-3 harboring transposon cluster was identified by using a Mash-based distance calculation for plasmids.
statements.note: The abstract identifies a blaKPC-3-harboring transposon cluster but never names the transposon family.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: All of the isolates carried a blaKPC-3 carbapenemase.
statements.evidence: All isolates carried a bla KPC-3 carbapenemase.
statements.note: The abstract states that all isolates, from both the ST307 and the ST101 cluster, carried a blaKPC-3 carbapenemase.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mash distance-based plasmid analysis did not support plasmid transfer between isolates but identified a transposon cluster shared by all of them.
statements.evidence: Further Mash distance-based plasmid analysis was not consistent with plasmid transfer due to genetic heterogeneity, but identified a transposon cluster across all isolates.
statements.note: The abstract reports that plasmid analysis was inconsistent with plasmid transfer yet found a transposon cluster across all isolates.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: The SPG20 + MGMT and SPG20 + ALX4 combinations reached AUCs of 0.994 and 0.990, respectively.
statements.evidence: Other combinations, such as SPG20 + MGMT and SPG20 + ALX4, also exhibited high accuracy (AUC = 0.994 and 0.990, respectively).
statements.note: The abstract reports AUCs of 0.994 for SPG20 + MGMT and 0.990 for SPG20 + ALX4.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Combining SEPT9 and SPG20 methylation separated the 25 CRC patients from the 25 controls with an AUC of 1.00.
statements.evidence: The combination of SEPT9 and SPG20 achieved excellent discrimination between CRC patients and controls (AUC = 1.00).
statements.note: The abstract reports an AUC of 1.00 for the SEPT9 and SPG20 combination in this 25 versus 25 case-control set.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Adding further genes to a panel brought only marginal gains in diagnostic accuracy, pointing to redundancy in larger panels.
statements.evidence: The inclusion of additional genes provided marginal diagnostic improvement, suggesting redundancy in larger panels.
statements.note: The abstract states that including additional genes gave marginal improvement, suggesting redundancy in larger panels.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The methylation panel detected early-stage CRC as accurately as late-stage disease.
statements.evidence: A pilot case-control study was conducted with 50 participants, comprising 25 confirmed CRC patients and 25 colonoscopy-verified CRC-free controls.
statements.note: The abstract gives no stage breakdown of the 25 CRC patients and reports no stage-specific performance.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within three days of sepsis onset, NGS-based diagnostics were positive in 70.5% of 491 septic patients, compared with 19.4% for blood cultures.
statements.evidence: The positivity rate of NGS-based diagnostics (NGS+) for 491 septic patients was 70.5% compared to positive BCs (BC+) with 19.4% within the first three days after sepsis onset.
statements.note: The abstract reports positivity rates of 70.5% for NGS and 19.4% for blood cultures in 491 patients within the first three days.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Based on the expert panel's recommendations, knowledge of NGS pathogen findings would have changed anti-infective treatment in 32.6% of all patients.
statements.evidence: additional knowledge of NGS-based pathogen findings would have resulted in anti-infective treatment adaptations in 32.6% of all patients
statements.note: The abstract reports that NGS findings would have led to anti-infective treatment adaptations in 32.6% of all patients.

statements.label: contradicted
statements.basis: Patients who were NGS-positive but blood-culture-negative, and thus potentially inadequately treated, had worse outcomes.
statements.evidence: Potentially inadequately treated NGS+/blood culture negative (BC-) patients showed worse outcomes.
statements.note: The abstract reports worse, not better, outcomes for potentially inadequately treated NGS-positive, blood-culture-negative patients.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: NGS results were available to clinicians sooner than blood culture results.
statements.evidence: The positivity rate of NGS-based diagnostics (NGS+) for 491 septic patients was 70.5% compared to positive BCs (BC+) with 19.4% within the first three days after sepsis onset.
statements.note: The abstract compares how often each method was positive, not how quickly results were returned; turnaround time is never reported.
